subject: File permissions + separation of R code from display HTML

messages.author: 596788cb1219e353
messages.subject: File permissions + separation of R code from display HTML
parts:
First, there have been posts about file permissions. Look among your
apache configuration files (envvars, apache2.conf, or httpd.conf).
You might find assignments to two symbols: APACHE_RUN_USER and
APACHE_RUN_GROUP. These can be used to assign the ownership of the
images directory. On my machine, both user and group are www-data .
Once the ownership is correct then file permissions can be tightened
to disallow world access.

Second. A highly desirable feature for any software package is
separation of display from content, client code from server code.
I've been experimenting with the r-script Apache handler with setting
"RHandler brew::brew". What I was after is the ability to separate
all of the R code into R-specific files. It turns out that brew
treats ordinary html as a pass through and that this goal is more or
less achievable.

I've rewritten the useR2007 example so that it's main entry is a
legitimate, brew-free html page.

# diff useR2007.rhtml useR2007.html
1d0
< <% setContentType('text/html') %>
46c45
< <div id="plot"><% brew('/var/www/brew/useR2007/useR2007plot.rhtml')
%></div>
---
> <div id="plot"></div>
54,56c53,55
< <div class="clearfix"><label>1-year Survival Rate:</label><input
type="text" name="p1" value="<%=p1%>"></input></div>
< <div class="clearfix"><label>3-year Survival Rate:</label><input
type="text" name="p2" value="<%=p2%>"></input>
< <div class="clearfix"><label>Treatment Effect Start Month:</
label><input type="text" name="mo" value="<%=mo%>"></input>
---
> <div class="clearfix"><label>1-year Survival Rate:</label><input type="text" name="p1"></input></div>
> <div class="clearfix"><label>3-year Survival Rate:</label><input type="text" name="p2"></input>
> <div class="clearfix"><label>Treatment Effect Start Month:</label><input type="text" name="mo"></input>
71a71,78
> <script type="text/javascript">
> window.addEventListener('load', function() {
> document.getElementsByName('p1')[0].value = '0.95';
> document.getElementsByName('p2')[0].value = '0.80';
> document.getElementsByName('mo')[0].value = '10';
> RePlot();
> }, false);
> </script>

The initial values to the textfields and the associated graphics are
initialized by adding an 'onload' event listener at the very bottom of
the page (just above the </body> tag). The R graphs are drawn by
invoking RPlot(), the action target of the input button. So,
initialization is no longer a special case.

My bet is that instead of HTML, I could have used PHP or Perl and
nothing will change. If that does not work, we can probably change
brew to treat .php or .pl files as pass throughs, too.

parts:
Hi Allan,

Thanks for the example. Reading this brought up a question I played
with a while ago:

What is a good way of combining php (or any other server side
scripting) with R/RApache? I was trying to embed some R calculations
in a site that is otherwise mostly php based. Since I have all the
queries etc. done from php I wanted to seperate the R part. I ended up
doing a Curl to th R script and returning the values I needed in the
php script as a json object. But, I reckon that is not the most
favorable solution of intergrating the two.

Would you have any advice here? Do you think the <% brew('... approach
would work for this server side intergration as well?

Cheers,

Maurits

messages.author: 596788cb1219e353
messages.subject: Re: File permissions + separation of R code from display HTML
parts:
Hi Maurits,

The <% brew(...) is only for initialization and can definitely be
done away with. The sample code is artificial in that it only ships
scalar parameters from client to server. This blog had something to
offer: http://wezfurlong.org/blog/2006/nov/http-post-from-php-without-curl
.

In general and as things stand now, the flow for a model application
might be
(1) Client requests data with parameters used to format a SQL query.
(2) Server executes the query and ships the returned data to client.
(3) Client requests plot using Ajax and has to ship the data back to
the server to get processed by R.
(4) R returns plots and text.

If the data size is > 1K this is an undesirable amount of network
traffic. I've been thinking about this for days -- I'm more of a Java/
C slob than a PHP wizard.

To remove the overhead and the copies on the client, I'm looking into
PHP include statements and globally scoped variables (
http://php.net/manual/en/language.variables.scope.php ). The data
flow would resemble:
(1) Client requests data with parameters used to format a SQL query.
(2) Server executes the query and stores the data on behalf of the
client in a globally visible variable.
(3) Client requests plot using Ajax (no data send necessary).
(4) R returns with plots and text.

There is one more problem to consider. RApache and R are generating
files on disk. In the sample application these are PNG files in the
'images' directory. Each click of the RePlot button in the sample
application useR2007 generates a PNG file that consumes 35K of disk
space. A site that has 100K users, each of whom clicks 25 files into
existence, would accumulate 83 gigabytes of such files.

A cron job should be cleaning these PNG files up?

Or another alternative would be to use the FilesMatch directive in
your apache config:
<Directory /dir>
<FilesMatch "\.rhtml$">
SetHandler r-script
RHandler brew::brew
</FilesMatch>
</Directory>

That way, all scripts with an ending .rhtml only get processed via brew.

Jeff

Sure.

> and while I'm on a mission to get to writing more education/tutorial
> material, I can't quite get to that yet.
>
> Thanks,
>
> Jeff
>
>
>
> On Sat, Oct 2, 2010 at 6:59 PM, Allan Jacobs <jacobsallans...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Hi Maurits,
>
> > The <% brew(...)  is only for initialization and can definitely be
> > done away with. The sample code is artificial in that it only ships
> > scalar parameters from client to server.  This blog had something to
> > offer:http://wezfurlong.org/blog/2006/nov/http-post-from-php-without-curl
> > .
>
> > In general and as things stand now, the flow for a model application
> > might be
> > (1) Client requests data with parameters used to format a SQL query.
> > (2) Server executes the query and ships the returned data to client.
> > (3) Client requests plot using Ajax and has to ship the data back to
> > the server to get processed by R.
> > (4) R returns plots and text.
>
> > If the data size is > 1K this is an undesirable amount of network
> > traffic.  I've been thinking about this for days -- I'm more of a Java/
> > C slob than a PHP wizard.
>
> > To remove the overhead and the copies on the client, I'm looking into
> > PHP include statements and globally scoped variables (
> >http://php.net/manual/en/language.variables.scope.php).  The data
> > flow would resemble:
> > (1) Client requests data with parameters used to format a SQL query.
> > (2) Server executes the query and stores the data on behalf of the
> > client in a globally visible variable.
> > (3) Client requests plot using Ajax (no data send necessary).
> > (4) R returns with plots and text.
>
> > There is one more problem to consider.  RApache and R are generating
> > files on disk.  In the sample application these are PNG files in the
> > 'images' directory.  Each click of the RePlot button in the sample
> > application useR2007 generates a PNG file that consumes 35K of disk
> > space.  A site that has 100K users, each of whom clicks 25 files into
> > existence, would accumulate 83 gigabytes of such files.
>
> > A cron job should be cleaning these PNG files up?
